clips.text_zh: 有4仔連登狗2014年DOGE銀包都hack返入去，730,000粒，即係6萬美金，問點投資好。ok 我啲prop firm都未過，睇人哋執到金真係wtf。
clips.text_en_b1: An anon hacked into his own 2014 Dogecoin wallet and recovered 730,000 DOGE, worth about $60,000 USD. He is now asking /biz/ where to invest the money, since real estate is too expensive in his area. He thinks a fixer-upper might work, but wants suggestions from the board.

signal.rationale: OP is a recovery story plus alloc question, no directional setup

clips.text_en_b2: An anon on /biz/ managed to crack his own long-dormant 2014 Dogecoin wallet and recover roughly 730,000 DOGE, which works out to around $60,000 at current prices. Although the figure sounds modest, he's treating it as a windfall and is now crowdsourcing investment ideas from the board. Because property is out of reach locally, he's leaning toward a fixer-upper, though he's clearly torn between playing it safe and chasing a quick return.
clips.text_en_c1: An anonymous poster on /biz/ has regained access to a dormant Dogecoin wallet originally set up back in 2014, recovering approximately 730,000 DOGE, which at prevailing rates translates to roughly $60,000 USD. Now that the coins are finally liquid, the thread has pivoted to investment strategy, particularly given that local property prices in his region remain prohibitively high. He is weighing whether a fixer-upper property might offer reasonable returns, though other anons are weighing in with alternative allocations. The general sentiment oscillates between cautious optimism and disbelief that an 11-year-old forgotten wallet has suddenly yielded a meaningful windfall for someone who has evidently struggled with prop firm evaluations up to…
clips.text_en_c2: An anonymous /biz/ user has reportedly regained access to a Dogecoin wallet left untouched since 2014, recovering approximately 730,000 DOGE, presently valued at around US$60,000. Rather than treating the windfall as an occasion for unbridled celebration, he has solicited investment advice from the board: local property prices are prohibitively high, although he believes that a dilapidated property in need of renovation might still prove viable after a properly scrutinised appraisal. The thread’s response is less a coherent portfolio strategy than a chorus of half-serious proposals, black humour, and warnings that cryptocurrency’s notorious volatility makes financial certainty elusive. The underlying irony is unmistakable: the money was recovered from an account effectively abandoned, yet deciding how to preserve it may prove considerably harder than obtaining it.

clips.text_zh: 有4仔問買Cybercab放落Tesla Robotaxi network做被動收入。lol 真係信晒Elon？btw 我自己CFD都輸緊，唔好再諗被動收入🙏
clips.text_en_b1: An anon on /biz/ is asking for a redpill on buying Tesla Cybercabs and putting them to work on the Tesla Robotaxi network for passive income. He sees it as a way to make money while he sleeps. The thread is asking whether the unit economics and software rollout actually work.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ thread on Tesla Cybercab passive income

signal.rationale: OP is buying Cybercab units, implicitly bullish on Tesla Robotaxi rollout

clips.text_en_b2: An anon on /biz/ is seriously weighing whether he should pick up a few Tesla Cybercabs and feed them into the Robotaxi network, hoping the whole thing runs itself while he sleeps. While the passive-income pitch does sound appealing on paper, the thread is busy tearing apart the unit economics, doubting the software rollout timeline, and generally roasting anyone who takes Elon Musk's promises at face value.
clips.text_en_c1: A /biz/ thread is soliciting input on the viability of purchasing Tesla's forthcoming Cybercab units and deploying them across the Robotaxi network as a form of passive income. The original poster frames the proposition as a hands-off revenue stream, ostensibly generating returns while he sleeps, and is requesting what he terms a redpill on the underlying unit economics. Other contributors have grown notably sceptical, questioning whether the software rollout will actually materialise on schedule or whether the projections constitute little more than speculative vapour. Given that I am currently bleeding money on CFD positions myself, I am hardly in a position to sermonise, though passive income remains a pipe dream.
clips.text_en_c2: An anonymous /biz/ contributor is seeking a characteristically forthright assessment of whether purchasing Tesla’s proposed Cybercab and placing it on the company’s Robotaxi network could constitute a credible source of largely passive income. His attraction is obvious: revenue generated by an autonomously operating asset, while its owner sleeps, offers an appealing answer to the perennial problem of making money without continuously trading time for money. The discussion, however, is properly sceptical, since the proposition rests not merely on vehicle demand but upon uncertain unit economics, regulatory approval, utilisation rates, maintenance liabilities, and the successful deployment of software that has not yet been demonstrated at fleet scale. Buying the car may be easy; earning a dependable return is another matter entirely.

clips.text_zh: 4仔話Hinton 2016年話AI 5年內取代放射科醫生，10年後唔止無被取代，需求仲多咗、人工仲高。即係連Elon都會睇走眼，我考HKIE都未驚住俾AI搶🙏
clips.text_en_b1: An anon on /g/ points out that in 2016, the godfather of AI Geoffrey Hinton predicted AI would replace radiologists within 5 years. Ten years later, there are more radiologists now, in higher demand, and earning higher salaries than in 2016. The thread then says Elon Musk is next to embarrass himself on the world stage.
clips.source_hint: /g/ thread on Hinton's failed radiologist prediction
clips.text_en_b2: An anon on /g/ dug up a famous 2016 clip of Geoffrey Hinton insisting AI would wipe out radiology jobs within five years. Despite that bold prediction, demand for radiologists has actually climbed, and their salaries have grown substantially over the past decade. The thread takes grim satisfaction in the failed forecast and jokingly nominates Elon Musk as the next big name likely to embarrass himself.
clips.text_en_c1: A /g/ poster has resurfaced a 2016 prediction by Geoffrey Hinton, widely regarded as the godfather of modern AI, in which he confidently asserted that artificial intelligence would render radiologists obsolete within five years. Roughly a decade on, the profession has not merely survived but has flourished, with demand, headcount and remuneration all trending markedly upward relative to 2016 baselines. The thread interprets this as yet another high-profile forecast that has spectacularly failed to materialise, suggesting that even figures such as Elon Musk, whose public pronouncements on automation routinely overshoot reality, are liable to comparable embarrassment.
clips.text_en_c2: A /g/ user has drawn attention to a prediction made by Geoffrey Hinton, widely regarded as a principal architect of modern artificial intelligence, who said in 2016 that AI could replace radiologists within five years. Roughly a decade on, the profession has not vanished; indeed, radiologists remain in greater demand and command higher salaries than they did in 2016. The discrepancy is instructive, because it demonstrates how technological capability can be confused with immediate occupational displacement: an algorithm may perform a narrow diagnostic task with remarkable proficiency without assuming the legal accountability, contextual judgement, and capacity for anomalous-case reasoning that define the clinical role. The thread consequently treats Hinton’s forecast as another example of intelligent people overestimating how rapidly institutions adapt.

clips.text_zh: 4仔/pol/問點解而家age gap突然變得好似犯咗罪咁。thx 我30單身一個都唔理，仲邊有心情理呢啲🧐 錢先係我而家嘅全部
clips.text_en_b1: An anon on /pol/ asks why age gaps in relationships have suddenly become so controversial. He is confused because older men dating younger women used to be normal in media and history. The thread debates whether this is a real cultural shift or just louder online voices.
clips.source_hint: /pol/ thread asking why age gaps are now controversial
clips.text_en_b2: An anon on /pol/ is genuinely puzzled about why age-gap relationships have suddenly become such a contentious issue, given that older men paired with younger women were once celebrated in film, literature, and royal history. While some users argue this reflects a genuine cultural shift, others insist it's simply louder online discourse and not a real change in actual behavior.
clips.text_en_c1: An anonymous user on /pol/ has raised the question of why age-gap relationships have, seemingly overnight, acquired the status of a moral transgression in contemporary discourse. He observes that, historically, older men partnering with considerably younger women was a fixture of literature, cinema and royal lineage alike, and he struggles to identify the precise cultural mechanism that has transformed what was once unremarkable into something requiring public apology. Contributors are divided as to whether this reflects a genuine and substantive shift in societal values or merely the disproportionate amplification of vocal minorities online.
clips.text_en_c2: An anonymous /pol/ user has asked why age-disparate relationships, particularly those involving an older man and a younger woman, are now treated as though they were intrinsically scandalous. His confusion is rooted in the fact that such pairings were once commonplace throughout history, literature, and popular culture, where they were frequently presented without the moral disquiet that surrounds them today. The ensuing debate considers whether this apparent change reflects a substantive cultural reevaluation or merely the amplification of conspicuous online minorities. Some argue that increased awareness of power imbalances and vulnerabilities has made romantic age gaps more difficult to romanticise uncritically; others see the controversy as a contemporary fashion, promoted by discourse that confuses visibility with consensus.

clips.text_zh: Riot設計又俾人post上4仔/v/，btw Dragami Games宣佈Lollipop Chainsaw Sequel會喺TGS 2026出，仲有得試玩。lol 我都仲未上分，睇下game先👍
clips.text_en_b1: Dragami Games announced on X that the Lollipop Chainsaw Sequel will be both revealed and playable at TGS 2026. The original 2012 cult action game is getting a follow-up showfloor demo. The /v/ thread is collecting reactions and old fan memories ahead of the official trailer.
clips.source_hint: /v/ thread on Lollipop Chainsaw Sequel at TGS 2026
clips.text_en_b2: Dragami Games revealed on X that the long-awaited Lollipop Chainsaw sequel will be both officially unveiled and made playable at Tokyo Game Show 2026, offering fans a first proper hands-on look. Since the 2012 original earned a devoted cult following despite middling sales, the announcement sent /v/ into a frenzy. The thread is already swapping nostalgic memories while bracing for whatever the new trailer delivers.
clips.text_en_c1: Dragami Games has officially confirmed via X that the long-anticipated Lollipop Chainsaw sequel will receive both its formal unveiling and a playable build at the Tokyo Game Show in 2026. The original 2012 title, which cultivated a devoted cult following on the strength of its irreverent tone and cheerleader-zombie premise, is consequently returning to the showfloor with a hands-on demo preceding whatever trailer assets are eventually released. The corresponding /v/ thread has accordingly morphed into a repository of reminiscences, with veteran fans unearthing decade-old screenshots, recounting the game's notoriously campy dialogue and speculating as to whether Dragami can recapture that particular brand of tongue-in-cheek absurdity that defined its predecessor.
clips.text_en_c2: Dragami Games has announced through X that the forthcoming Lollipop Chainsaw sequel will receive its first substantial public presentation at the Tokyo Game Show in 2026, where attendees will apparently have the opportunity not only to witness its unveiling but also to try the game for themselves. The news is particularly significant because the original 2012 release, though never an unqualified mainstream success, cultivated an unusually devoted following through its flamboyant premise, eccentric humour, and conspicuously committed performances. For those fans, the show-floor demonstration represents something more meaningful than routine product marketing: it is the first tangible indication that Dragami understands what made the original memorable rather than merely reviving its name as a disposable nostalgia commodity. Naturally, /v/ has begun assembling the customary mixture of enthusiasm, scepticism, and affectionate recollections.

clips.text_en_b1: A /fit/ anon is 5'9, 160lbs, lifting for 2 years. He went from 140lbs skinnyfat to 200lbs bulk, then cut to current. His frame is bad so he over-emphasizes shoulders. Diet is 160p, 272c, 57f at 2293 kcal, 10k+ steps daily, plus occasional cardio. He wants advice on his next split and physique priorities.
clips.source_hint: /fit/ thread asking for physique and split advice at 5'9 160lb
clips.text_en_b2: A /fit/ anon stands 5'9 and currently sits at 160lbs after two full years of serious training. He started skinnyfat at 140lbs, ran an aggressive bulk up to 200lbs, and carefully cut back down to where he is now. Because his natural frame is on the narrow side, he overcompensates by hammering shoulders hard. His numbers read 160 protein, 272 carbs, 57 fat at 2,293 kcal, with 10k-plus steps daily.
clips.text_en_c1: A /fit/ contributor standing 5'9 and weighing in at 160lbs has documented a two-year transformation from a 140lb skinnyfat baseline through a dedicated bulk cycle peaking at 200lbs, followed by a disciplined cut to his present weight. Cognisant of his unfavourable frame, he has deliberately over-prioritised shoulder development to broaden his silhouette and offset narrower clavicles. His current regimen consists of 160g protein, 272g carbohydrates and 57g fat, totalling 2,293 kcal, supplemented by a daily commitment of 10,000-plus steps and sporadic cardio sessions. He is now soliciting feedback regarding optimal training split adjustments and which physique priorities warrant emphasis as he enters what he considers his next refinement phase.
clips.text_en_c2: A /fit/ user standing 5 feet 9 inches tall and weighing approximately 160 pounds has presented a two-year transformation that began at a markedly undermuscled 140 pounds. He subsequently bulked to 200 pounds before cutting back to his present weight, a sequence that produced visible development but left him dissatisfied with his overall proportions. Because he considers his underlying frame comparatively narrow, he has deliberately overemphasised deltoid work, evidently hoping that broader shoulders will create the illusion of a more imposing upper body. His daily intake is recorded as 160 grams of protein, 272 grams of carbohydrates, and 57 grams of fat, totalling 2,293 calories; he also reports walking more than 10,000 steps each day and incorporating occasional cardiovascular work.

clips.text_en_b2: Now that the third Index anime season has wrapped up, an /a/ anon has set himself the absurd mission of tracking down every single English physical volume of the Raildex franchise before he moves on. He's committed to collecting Index, Railgun, Astral Buddy, Accelerator, and Mental Out, and plans to stick around at least until the Index manga concludes its serialization run.
clips.text_en_c1: Now that the third season of the Railgun anime adaptation has concluded its broadcast run, a particularly devoted /a/ poster has declared his intention to acquire every English-language physical volume the broader Raildex franchise has ever produced. His shopping list encompasses the principal Railgun manga, the Astral Buddy and Accelerator spin-offs, the Mental Out side material and, eventually, the complete Index run in print. His stated rationale is straightforward: once the Index manga finally ceases serialisation and the franchise is definitively concluded, he will consider his collection architecturally complete and divest himself of further obligation.
clips.text_en_c2: With the third season of the A Certain Scientific Railgun anime now concluded, a committed /a/ reader has undertaken what he describes as a final campaign to complete his English-language physical collection. His intended purchases extend beyond Railgun itself to the closely related Astral Buddy and Accelerator series, as well as Mental Out, thereby assembling the franchise’s principal English releases in durable form. The promised endpoint, however, is contingent upon the eventual conclusion of the A Certain Magical Index manga: until its serialisation finally ends, the self-imposed moratorium remains technically incomplete. For the collector, this is less an impulsive shopping spree than a declaration of closure after years of fragmented publication, delayed localisation, and intermittent returns.
